chunks: We were told by Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Alawi, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from his brother Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Marwan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, orphaned His Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, in order for there to be none upon him to obey.

key_terms.أَيَّتَمَ: orphaned (caused to be without a guardian/father)

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah orphan the Prophet Muhammad according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq elucidates the divine wisdom behind the Prophet's death preceding the explicit designation of a permanent successor, describing it as Allah 'orphaning' him to prevent any human from claiming absolute obedience (*ta'ah mutlaqah*). This concept underscores the Shia distinction between the Prophet's unique status and the Imams, ensuring that while the Imams are infallible guides, they remain servants of God rather than objects of worship-like devotion, thereby preserving the purity of monotheism.

en.basel-kadem: 5.	We were told by Hamza bin Muhammed al-Alawi, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Abu’l-Abbas, Ahmad bin Muhammed al-Kufi, from Ali bin Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal, from his brother, Ahmad, from Muhammed bin Abdullah bin Marwan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, orphaned his Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, in order for there to be none upon him to obey.
